decisions.rationale: The author asks the recipient to complete and return cards.
evidence: Please enter the display-case numbers on the textile condition cards and return them to me.

decisions.rationale: The author directly promises future delivery without qualification.
evidence: I will send you the accession packets for the dune-grass seeds tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The earlier promise is withdrawn; the current delivery statement expresses hope.
evidence: Please disregard that assurance; we now hope to send them later in the week.

decisions.rationale: Scheduled future-progressive wording asserts a definite handover.
evidence: At 9 tomorrow morning, we will be handing over the updated tape inventory to the station librarian.

decisions.rationale: Delivery occurred in the completed past.
evidence: I delivered the community radio tape inventory last Tuesday.

decisions.rationale: Delivery depends on the casting becoming testable.
evidence: I will send its acoustic certificate when the casting is cool enough to test.

decisions.rationale: The author makes a firm promise about a separate ledger.
evidence: I will send you our completed cooperative graft ledger tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: An explicit promise assures receipt; the retraction concerns another item.
evidence: I can promise that you will receive the corrected cue sheets tomorrow.
My retraction concerned the restored picture master.

decisions.rationale: The author recalls an old promise without renewing it.
evidence: Last winter I promised to send the tape inventory by the end of that week.
I am recounting the old arrangement here.

decisions.rationale: The author assures future receipt of concrete work.
evidence: You will receive the completed tapestry condition cards from me by Thursday afternoon.

decisions.rationale: The passage describes completed work and existing documentation.
evidence: I repaired the split hem yesterday and handed the revised condition card to the registrar.

decisions.rationale: Receipt is assured before an event that serves as a deadline.
evidence: Before the first kite launches, you will have the printed course sketches from our organising team.

decisions.rationale: The author requests delivery from the recipient.
evidence: Could you send me the annotated cave-survey plates before the archive meeting?

decisions.rationale: The limestone delivery is firmly promised independently of the granite retraction.
evidence: I withdraw my promise to send the granite catalogue tomorrow.
I will send you the limestone sample catalogue tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The forecast is attributed to the cartographer, not newly asserted by the author.
evidence: The expedition cartographer expects her team to deliver the eastern-chamber plates next week.
That is her forecast, copied into my archive notes.

decisions.rationale: The promise is quoted from the grower and concerns her staff.
evidence: Mara, the grower, told me, "We will send the graft ledger on Monday."
Her 'we' refers to the nursery staff.

decisions.rationale: Both deliveries explicitly depend on approval.
evidence: If the quarry manager approves the sample list, I will send both catalogues on Friday.
Without that approval, neither will be sent.

decisions.rationale: Dispatch is described as already completed.
evidence: Yesterday I dispatched the accession packets for all twelve meadow collections.

decisions.rationale: The statement describes capability without committing to delivery.
evidence: I can export the piano's voicing records as a PDF.
That describes the workshop software's capability; I have not set a delivery date.

decisions.rationale: Delivery depends on survey readiness.
evidence: If the wind survey is ready tonight, I will get you the course sketches before tomorrow's launch.

decisions.rationale: An intention alone does not assure delivery.
evidence: I intend to send you the voicing records on Wednesday.

decisions.rationale: The author directly commits to a future inventory delivery.
evidence: I will deliver the music-tape inventory this Friday.

decisions.rationale: Survey readiness is an unresolved delivery dependency.
evidence: We will send the course sketches when the wind survey is ready.
The survey team has not finished its measurements.

decisions.rationale: The author asserts a definite handover at a scheduled event.
evidence: At Monday's inspection, I will hand you the acoustic certificate for bell B17.

decisions.rationale: The author's team firmly commits to delivery; the forecast concerns separate work.
evidence: Our archive team will deliver the western-passage map plates to you at Friday's briefing; the cartographer's forecast concerns the separate eastern survey.

decisions.rationale: The corrected statement firmly promises the reel-one cue sheet.
evidence: I will send the completed cue sheet for reel one on Friday.

decisions.rationale: Sandstone catalogue receipt is assured independently of the slate retraction.
evidence: You will receive the sandstone sample catalogue from our estimating team by noon Monday.
The slate catalogue is no longer promised for that date.

decisions.rationale: The briefing supplies a deadline for unconditional delivery.
evidence: I will deliver the regatta course sketches before the opening briefing.

decisions.rationale: The final explicit assurance resolves the earlier plan wording.
evidence: Our plan is to send the concert piano's voicing log at noon on Friday.
To be explicit, we will do so.

decisions.rationale: The author explicitly negates delivery and retracts the assurance.
evidence: I will not deliver the restoration cue sheets tomorrow; that earlier assurance was a mistake.

decisions.rationale: The author's team assures future receipt of the envelopes.
evidence: You will receive the matching accession envelopes from our curation team by noon tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The final reference to catalogue delivery leaves unresolved whether the condition covers only granite or also the initially firm limestone delivery.
evidence: Friday's handover: I will send the limestone catalogue; the granite catalogue will follow if the sample review passes.
That condition applies to the catalogue delivery.

decisions.rationale: The author's team directly commits to delivering its concrete ledger.
evidence: My coordination team owns the consolidated graft ledger.
We will deliver it to you on Monday.

decisions.rationale: The author records the donor's promise without adopting it.
evidence: The donor wrote, "I will send the accession envelopes on Thursday."
I am recording her words here so the intake desk knows what she said.

decisions.rationale: The author makes a new unconditional delivery commitment.
evidence: I will send you the final cartographic plate tomorrow morning.

decisions.rationale: A scheduled handover is assured for the tested bell, separate from the cooling delay.
evidence: For the tested bell, our team will be handing over the signed acoustic certificate at 10 tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The explicit promise assures delivery despite possible disagreement about the annotations.
evidence: Still, I can promise that I will deliver the voicing records tomorrow.

decisions.rationale: The delivery assertion belongs to the grower and is merely copied by the author.
evidence: She says she will deliver it on Thursday.
I have only copied that statement into the cooperative's notes.

decisions.rationale: The author's team unconditionally promises future delivery of condition cards.
evidence: Our conservation team will send you the matching condition cards tomorrow, and the cards will include the treatment photographs.

decisions.rationale: Delivery explicitly depends on uncertain cooling progress.
evidence: If the bronze has cooled enough for the resonance test, we will deliver the acoustic certificate on Tuesday.
The cooling rate is still uncertain.
